newsitem.title: CHINA: China predicts minerals discoveries in southwest.
newsitem.headline: China predicts minerals discoveries in southwest.

text.p: Chinese minerals officials are planning to step up exploration efforts in a mountainous area of the southwestern province of Yunnan that is believed to be rich in copper, silver and gold, the China Daily said on Monday.

Copper reserves in the "three rivers" area near the Nujiang, Lancang and Jinsha rivers could total more than 10 million tonnes, the newspaper quoted Ministry of Geological and Mineral Resources officials as saying.

Mineral deposits uncovered so far had strengthened the ministry's confidence in the chances of finding 5,000 tonnes of silver reserves and 50 tonnes of gold reserves in the 160,000 square km area by the end of the century, it said.
It gave no details of the estimated reserves or how quickly officials expected to begin exploiting them.
The geological ministry had joined the State Planning Commission to draft a plan aimed at intensifying prospecting efforts in the mountainous area, it said.
Preferential policies would be introduced to accelerate exploration and a comprehensive resources report on the area would be produced over the next five to eight years, it said.
